resources.string: Needs a shell; the firmware\'s own apps lose the wheel keys meanwhile
Add Dashwheel to the sleep whitelist of the unit (its BootControl app, or the ROM mod settings). Otherwise the firmware stops it when the ignition goes off.
The MediaTek background saver stops Dashwheel at ignition off. Dashwheel turns it off itself, at each boot, once it may write secure settings.
In the factory settings of the unit. The unit then starts normally instead of killing apps before its fast sleep.
The firmware keeps three lists of apps allowed to start, run behind and survive the sleep. Dashwheel adds itself to them with root.
